subject: Launch window: phased per-token discount & monthly step-up commit proposal
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@launchpad.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@launchpad.com
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: Launchpad launch window — need ramp/discount structure

Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the KV caching behavior. We have an internal launch slated for Feb and need to lock a committed plan that balances predictable costs with headroom for the launch surge.

Can you send a clear monthly commit / step-up schedule (per-token tiers) for an initial 3-month launch window, plus any short-term surge credits or true-up mechanics? Procurement wants an example price schedule we can include in the SOW. Also flag any minimums or hard cutoffs that would affect our traffic pattern (we expect a 6x traffic spike week-of-launch).

High level:
- Expected baseline: ~1.2B tokens/month in Jan (pre-launch)
- Launch month (Feb): likely 7–8B tokens
- Post-launch steady state (Mar): 2.5–3B tokens

If you can, attach a sample ramp and call out any one-time onboarding credits for early-stage customers.

—Michael
Director of Product
Launchpad Inc

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@launchpad.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launchpad launch window — need ramp/discount structure

Michael — thanks, this is very helpful context. Attached is a suggested phased commit and per-token discount schedule geared specifically for a short high-throughput launch: "LP-Ramp-Proposal-2025.xlsx" and our summary pricing sheet. Highlights below (summarized):

- Month 0 (Jan) baseline: commit 1.25B tokens — unit price $0.00120/token
- Month 1 (Feb) launch step-up: commit 8.0B tokens — unit price steps to $0.00095/token for volume above baseline
- Month 2 (Mar) step-down: commit 3.0B tokens — unit price $0.00105/token

Discount structure: tiered, per-token, applied to consumption per month. We can front-load a 10% launch credit that applies to overage above the committed monthly total for the first two billing cycles (to cover burst).

True-up / overage: monthly true-up at actual consumption; overage charged at published per-token rates unless covered by launch credit. We can include a one-time onboarding credit of $15k if you execute a 12-month commitment (reduces first invoice).

Constraints and notes:
- We require a 30% headroom cap for autoscaling fallback if you exceed 10x the monthly committed tokens — above which we reserve right to throttle or route to alternate lower-cost model variants.
- Surge credits are one-time and applied at invoice-line level (not refundable).

I've put conservative numbers in the attached sheet and flagged two optional concession points for internal review: a bigger onboarding credit vs shortening minimum commit term.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the procurement contact and preferred SOW template.
2) If the numbers look good, we'll produce a contract exhibit with the monthly table and DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: LP-Ramp-Proposal-2025.xlsx (Excel), redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (PDF)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launchpad launch window — need ramp/discount structure

Looping in a quick suggestion based on similar launch deals: we can offer an alternate ramp that reduces Month 1 commit (from 8B to 6B) in exchange for a 9-month minimum instead of 12 and a smaller onboarding credit ($10k). That helps our capacity planning and still gives Launchpad protection for the spike via the 10% launch credit.

Operational ask: can we mark the launch month as an "elastic allowance" in the contract exhibit (line item) so ops can apply the credit automatically? If legal/procurement prefers explicit true-up language, we should include both an allowance and the true-up calculation.

If you want me to, I can draft the exhibit and the alternate numbers.

—Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@launchpad.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@launchpad.com
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launchpad launch window — need ramp/discount structure

Neha, Rishi — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from procurement and finance before we proceed to SOW: 

1) Does the per-token "unit price" apply to all token types (prompt + completion), or do you separate prompt vs completion rates? We need explicit line items.
2) Please confirm the mechanics of the 10% launch credit (applies only to overage, or entire consumption up to the step-up level?).
3) Is the onboarding credit applied as a cash credit or as an invoice-level credit (we prefer invoice-level for bookkeeping).

Procurement also asked for a draft SOW exhibit in Word (they prefer docx) and a sample DPA. Can you send the exhibit and the contract exhibit with the alternate ramp (6B launch / 9-month min) that Rishi proposed? We should review legal before DocuSign.

If everything looks OK, we can target signature the week of Dec 15.

Thanks — Lisa
VP, Operations
Launchpad Inc

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@launchpad.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2025 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launchpad launch window — need ramp/discount structure

Lisa — quick follow up from pricing/legal:

1) We bill per-token across prompt + completion; contract exhibit will show prompt and completion separately for transparency, but the effective blended unit price in the proposal is the one used for invoice calc. We'll include both lines in the docx exhibit.
2) Launch credit: applies only to overage above the committed monthly total for the first two billing cycles. We'll explicitly state that in the exhibit and sample DPA.
3) Onboarding credit: invoice-level credit (applied against first invoice).

Concession: Approved to offer the alternate ramp Rishi suggested (6B Feb commit / 9-month minimum) with a $10k onboarding credit. We will also include an "elastic allowance" line item of up to 20% of the monthly commit for the launch month to reduce manual exceptions — that allowance consumes the 10% launch credit first.

I'll attach a draft docx exhibit and a redlined clause for true-up language. Neha / Rishi — once you confirm, I'll generate the DocuSign envelope (DocuSign://envelope/DS-99827) and share with Lisa/procurement.

—Aditya
Pricing & Packaging Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
